The arrow of the dipole moment \vec{p} is along the oblique line from -q toward +q, that is, pointing to the upper right. The observation point is on the upper right of the same straight line, at a distance r from O along the direction of \vec{p}, and the problem gives r \gg a. Reasoning: Take the direction along \vec{p} as the positive direction, then -q is located at x=-a, +q is located at x=+a, and the observation point is located at x=r. The distance from +q to the observation point is r-a, and its electric-field direction is along the positive direction; the distance from -q to the observation point is r+a, and its electric-field direction points toward -q, that is, along the negative direction. Therefore, by Coulomb superposition, E_p=\frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\left[\frac{q}{(r-a)^2}-\frac{q}{(r+a)^2}\right]. Combining the fractions: E_p=\frac{q}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\frac{(r+a)^2-(r-a)^2}{(r^2-a^2)^2} =\frac{q}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\frac{4ra}{(r^2-a^2)^2}. Since r\gg a, therefore (r^2-a^2)^2\approx r^4, so E_p\approx \frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\frac{4qa}{r^3}. Also p=2aq, so 4qa=2p, obtaining E_p=\frac{2p}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 r^3}, with the direction along \vec{p}.

raw_record.question_text:
Calculate the electric field intensity $\vec{E}_{p}$ at a distance $r$ from an ideal electric dipole $\vec{p}$ at the origin $\mathrm{O}$ along the direction of $\vec{p}$ in Figure 2.

$p=2aq, \quad r \gg a$

method.method_draft: First describe the diagram: the dipole lies on a slanted straight line with charge -q on the lower-left side, charge +q on the upper-right side, O between them, each charge a distance a from O, and the observation point located further along the same line in the direction of the dipole moment vector p. From the text use p = 2aq and r >> a. Compute the electric field at the observation point by Coulomb superposition along the dipole axis: the +q field points along +p with distance r-a, while the -q field points opposite +p with distance r+a. Thus E = (1/4πε0)[q/(r-a)^2 - q/(r+a)^2] along p. Combine the fractions to get (1/4πε0) q[4ra/(r^2-a^2)^2], then use r >> a so (r^2-a^2)^2 ≈ r^4, giving E ≈ (1/4πε0)(4qa/r^3). Substitute p = 2aq to obtain E_p = 2p/(4πε0 r^3), directed along p.
method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：图中电偶极子位于一条从左下到右上的斜直线上，左下端是电荷 -q，右上侧是电荷 +q，原点 O 位于两电荷之间；从 O 到 -q 和 +q 的距离都标为 a。偶极矩 \vec{p} 的箭头沿斜线由 -q 指向 +q，即指向右上方。观察点在同一直线的右上方，沿 \vec{p} 方向距 O 的距离为 r，且题给 r \gg a。

推理：取沿 \vec{p} 的方向为正方向，则 -q 位于 x=-a，+q 位于 x=+a，观察点位于 x=r。+q 到观察点的距离为 r-a，其电场方向沿正方向；-q 到观察点的距离为 r+a，其电场方向指向 -q，即沿负方向。因此由库仑叠加得
E_p=\frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\left[\frac{q}{(r-a)^2}-\frac{q}{(r+a)^2}\right].
合并分式：
E_p=\frac{q}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\frac{(r+a)^2-(r-a)^2}{(r^2-a^2)^2}
=\frac{q}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\frac{4ra}{(r^2-a^2)^2}.
由于 r\gg a，故 (r^2-a^2)^2\approx r^4，于是
E_p\approx \frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\frac{4qa}{r^3}.
又 p=2aq，所以 4qa=2p，得到
E_p=\frac{2p}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 r^3}，方向沿 \vec{p}。
method.model_answer: \vec{E}_p=\frac{2p}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 r^3}\,\hat{p}，即大小 E_p=\frac{2p}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 r^3}，方向沿 \vec{p}。

V = (1/(4πε0))[q/(r-a) - q/(r+a)]
= (1/(4πε0)) q[(r+a)-(r-a)]/[(r-a)(r+a)]
= (1/(4πε0)) 2qa/(r^2-a^2)。

V ≈ (1/(4πε0)) 2qa/r^2 = p/(4πε0 r^2)。
轴向电场为 E_r = -dV/dr，因此
E_p = -d/dr[p/(4πε0 r^2)] = 2p/(4πε0 r^3)。
方向为正 p 方向。

ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Calculate the electric field intensity $\vec{E}_{p}$ at a distance $r$ from an ideal electric dipole $\vec{p}$ at the origin $\mathrm{O}$ along the direction of $\vec{p}$ in Figure 2. $p=2aq, \quad r \gg a$
ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot:
Image description: In the figure, the electric dipole is located on an oblique straight line from the lower left to the upper right; the lower-left end is the charge -q, and the upper-right side is the charge +q; the origin O is located between the two charges; the distances from O to -q and +q are both marked as a. The arrow of the dipole moment \vec{p} is along the oblique line from -q toward +q, that is, pointing to the upper right. The observation point is on the upper right of the same straight line, at a distance r from O along the direction of \vec{p}, and the problem gives r \gg a.

Reasoning: Take the direction along \vec{p} as the positive direction, then -q is located at x=-a, +q is located at x=+a, and the observation point is located at x=r. The distance from +q to the observation point is r-a, and its electric-field direction is along the positive direction; the distance from -q to the observation point is r+a, and its electric-field direction points toward -q, that is, along the negative direction. Therefore, by Coulomb superposition,
E_p=\frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\left[\frac{q}{(r-a)^2}-\frac{q}{(r+a)^2}\right].
Combining the fractions:
E_p=\frac{q}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\frac{(r+a)^2-(r-a)^2}{(r^2-a^2)^2}
=\frac{q}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\frac{4ra}{(r^2-a^2)^2}.
Since r\gg a, therefore (r^2-a^2)^2\approx r^4, so
E_p\approx \frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\frac{4qa}{r^3}.
Also p=2aq, so 4qa=2p, obtaining
E_p=\frac{2p}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 r^3}, with the direction along \vec{p}.
